html:
Sunni Islam is the largest branch of Islam, followed by about 85 to 90 percent of Muslims. Its name comes from the sunna, the example of the Prophet Muhammad, and Sunnis call themselves the people of the sunna and the community.

The split with Shia Islam began over who should lead after Muhammad's death in 632. Sunnis honour the first four caliphs, Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman and Ali, as the rightly guided caliphs; the Shia hold that Ali should have come first.

Sunni Islam has no priestly hierarchy. Authority lies with scholars who interpret the Quran and the hadith, the reports of the Prophet's words and deeds. Al-Bukhari's collection is the most trusted of its six canonical hadith books. Four schools of law, the Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi'i and Hanbali, took shape by the 900s, and each prevails in different regions. Al-Ghazali brought Sufi mysticism into the mainstream. Cairo's Al-Azhar, founded by the Shia Fatimids but Sunni since Saladin, is its leading centre of learning. In 2005 the Amman Message had scholars recognise all four Sunni schools and the main Shia ones as Muslim.
sum: Sunni Islam is the largest branch of Islam, followed by about 85 to 90 percent of Muslims. Its name comes from the sunna, the example of the Prophet Muhammad, and Sunnis call themselves the people of the sunna and the community.
